q: Under Section 7.14, an architect must not appropriate or unduly take advantage of the ideas of another architect without:
o: Payment of a licensing fee to the UAP
Publication of the idea in a journal first
Express authority from the originating architect
A signed non-compete agreement
n: Section 7.14 bars appropriating the intellectual property or unduly taking advantage of another architect's ideas without express authority from the originating architect. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.14)

q: An architect wants a magazine feature showcasing a recently completed project. Under Section 3.5, which is prohibited?
o: Allowing the magazine to photograph the completed project
Being interviewed about the design process
Soliciting advertisements or other support toward the cost of a publication presenting his/her own work
Providing the magazine with factual project data
n: Section 3.5 prohibits soliciting (or permitting solicitation of) advertisements or support for the cost of a publication presenting the architect's own work, and bars paid endorsement advertising of construction materials/equipment. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.5)

q: Under Section 11 (Effectivity Clause), when does the Code take effect?
o: Immediately upon signing by the Board Chairman
Thirty (30) days after Senate ratification
On the first day of the following calendar year
After fifteen (15) days following its full and complete publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation
n: Section 11 provides the Resolution takes effect after fifteen (15) days following its full and complete publication in the Official Gazette or any daily newspaper of general circulation in the Philippines. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 11)

q: Under Section 7.8, an architect should refrain from associating with, or allowing use of his/her name by, which kind of enterprise?
o: Any enterprise that may negatively affect himself/herself or the architectural profession
Any enterprise that is a direct competitor
Any enterprise located outside the Philippines
Any enterprise not accredited by IAPOA, regardless of legitimacy
n: Section 7.8 requires refraining from association with, or allowing use of one's name by, any enterprise that may negatively affect the architect or the architectural profession. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.8)

q: According to the closing attestation of the resolution, in what city and on what date was the Code of Ethical Conduct done/signed?
o: Manila, on the 2nd day of January, 2006
Manila, on the 5th day of April, 2006
Cebu City, on the 15th day of April, 2006
Quezon City, on the 5th day of April, 2004
n: The resolution's closing attestation states it was done in the City of Manila, this 5th day of April, 2006. (Source: Board of Architecture Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Attestation)

q: Sections 4.11 and 4.12 together require the architect to do what regarding the timing and communication of project work?
o: Carry out work without undue delay within an agreed reasonable time limit, and keep the Client informed of progress and any issues affecting quality or cost
Report to the Client only upon project completion
Complete all work within 30 calendar days regardless of scope
Delegate all client communication to the contractor
n: Section 4.11 requires work without undue delay within an agreed reasonable time limit; Section 4.12 requires keeping the Client informed at all times of progress and of any issue affecting quality or cost. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Secs. 4.11-4.12)

q: Under Section 7.13, an architect's professional practice must abide by what kind of internal arrangements?
o: A single-person office structure only
An open-door policy with no formal procedures at all
Outsourcing all quality control to the client
Appropriate and effective internal procedures, including monitoring/review processes and sufficient qualified, supervised staff
n: Section 7.13 requires the architect's practice to have appropriate and effective internal procedures, including monitoring and review processes, and sufficient qualified and supervised staff to function efficiently. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.13)

q: Section 9 states that violators are liable under specific provisions of R.A. No. 9266 and Board Resolution No. 07, Series of 2004. Which provisions of R.A. No. 9266 are cited?
o: Sec. 30, Art. V and Sec. 31, Art. V
Sec. 23(f), Art. III and Sec. 29, Art. IV
Sec. 2, Art. I and Sec. 5, Art. II
Sec. 7(g), Art. II and Sec. 14, Art. I
n: Section 9 cites liability under Sec. 23(f), Art. III and Sec. 29, Art. IV of R.A. No. 9266, and the corresponding Sec. 23(f), Rule III and Sec. 29, Rule IV of Board Resolution No. 07, Series of 2004. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 9)

q: An architect offering services as an independent consultant is asked informally, with no official engagement yet, to name a fee. Under Section 7.16, what should the architect do?
o: Quote the maximum allowable fee to protect against under-pricing
Quote a low estimate immediately to attract the client
Decline to ever discuss fees informally under any circumstance
Not quote a fee without first receiving an official invitation to do so, and first obtain sufficient information on the project's nature and scope
n: Section 7.16 requires not quoting a fee without first receiving an official invitation, and having sufficient project information to prepare a clear fee proposal, protecting the Client and public from under-resourcing or underpricing. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.16)

q: Under Section 5.3, upon personal knowledge and inspection of nonconforming material, equipment, or workmanship, what must the architect do?
o: Wait until project completion to raise the issue
Immediately reject or condemn it, to avoid unnecessary delay and additional expense to the Contractor
Allow it to remain if the Client does not object
Refer the matter to a third-party engineer before acting
n: Section 5.3 requires immediate rejection or condemnation, upon personal knowledge and inspection, of material/equipment/workmanship not conforming to the Contract Documents, precisely to avoid unnecessary delay and additional expense. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.3)

q: Under Section 3.6, an architect may claim a professional specialization only if it is supported by which of the following?
o: Academic qualification, relevant track record, adequate professional resources, and peer sanction
A single completed project of that type
Approval from the client alone
A self-declared preference for that specialization
n: Section 3.6 bars deceiving the public as to competence; a specialization claim must be supported by academic qualification, track record of relevant expertise, adequate professional resources, and sanction by peers in the profession. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.6)

q: Under Section 10 (Separability Clause), what happens to the rest of the Code if one section or part is declared unconstitutional or invalid?
o: The entire Code is automatically voided
The Code must be re-ratified in its entirety by the UAP
The other sections or provisions not directly involved in the judgment remain unaffected, valid, and unimpaired
Only Article I remains in force
n: Section 10 provides that a declaration of unconstitutionality or invalidity of any section/part shall not affect, invalidate, or impair the other sections or provisions not directly involved in that judgment. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 10)

q: A proposed project appears financially or legally impracticable. Under Section 4.3, what must the architect do, even at the risk of losing the commission?
o: Proceed anyway to avoid losing the fee
Advise the Client against proceeding with the project
Say nothing and let the client discover the problem later
Refer the client to a different architect without explanation
n: Section 4.3 requires the architect to advise a Client against proceeding with a project of questionable practicability due to financial or legal conditions, even if it means losing the commission. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.3)

q: Who signed the Code of Ethical Conduct resolution as Chairman of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture?
o: Carlos G. Almelor
Leonor Tripon-Rosero
Eugene G. Gan
Miguel R. Caluza
n: The resolution was signed by Eugene G. Gan as Chairman, with Fernando L. Santos and Miguel R. Caluza as Members, attested to by Secretary Carlos G. Almelor, and approved by PRC Chairperson Leonor Tripon-Rosero. (Source: Board of Architecture Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Signatories)

q: An architect holds a personal investment in a materials supply business that could relate to a current Client's project. Under Section 4.9, what is required?
o: Nothing is required unless the Client discovers it independently
Transfer the investment to a family member instead of disclosing
Inform the Client of such a condition or situation
Keep it confidential since it is a personal matter
n: Section 4.9 requires the architect to remain free from financial/personal interests that could weaken his/her impartiality, and to inform the Client if any other business interest would relate to or affect the Client's interest. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.9)

q: An architect learns that a project has already been committed, though negotiations are ongoing, to another architect. Under Section 7.4, what is prohibited?
o: Discussing the project informally at a professional gathering
Merely inquiring about the project's status
Soliciting that project, under any circumstances or through any means
Referring the client to a third architect
n: Section 7.4 prohibits soliciting, by any means, a project already known to be previously committed to another architect, whether that commitment is still under negotiation or already definitely agreed. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.4)

q: What Board of Architecture issuance adopted and promulgated the Code of Ethical Conduct for Registered and Licensed Architects?
o: Resolution No. 07, Series of 2004
Resolution No. 03, Series of 2004
Resolution No. 01, Series of 2006
Resolution No. 02, Series of 2006
n: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture adopted and promulgated the Code through Resolution No. 02, Series of 2006. (Source: Board of Architecture Resolution No. 02, Series of 2006)

q: Under Section 7.17.4, what must the written commission agreement specify regarding compensation?
o: The contractor's markup percentage
The architect's personal income tax bracket
The fee or the method of calculating it
Only the Client's total project budget
n: Section 7.17.4 requires the written agreement to specify the fee or the method of calculating it. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.17.4)

q: Under Section 5.2, an architect must not knowingly do what regarding oversights or errors in the Contract Documents?
o: Correct them at the architect's own expense
Document them in the project file
Call upon the Contractor to remedy them to the Contractor's or Owner's financial disadvantage
Disclose them to the Client at all
n: Section 5.2 bars the architect from knowingly calling upon the Contractor to remedy oversights or errors in the Contract Documents to the Contractor's or Owner's financial disadvantage. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.2)

q: Under Section 5.1, what must an architect furnish the Contractor to help avoid unnecessary mistakes and extra costs?
o: A copy of the architect's own professional fee schedule
Access to the Client's financial records
Only verbal instructions during site visits
Clear, definite, and consistent information on all pertinent contract documents
n: Section 5.1 requires giving the Contractor every reasonable assistance by furnishing clear, definite, and consistent information on the contract documents. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.1)

q: Under Section 6.2, an architect must not seek commissions, discounts, fees, gifts, or favors from agents/firms handling building materials, and any market discounts obtained must be:
o: Credited to the Client
Donated to the IAPOA
Split evenly between the architect and the contractor
Kept by the architect as additional compensation
n: Section 6.2 bars seeking such commissions/discounts/gifts that would place the architect in a reciprocal frame of mind, and requires all market discounts be credited to the Client. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. V, Sec. 6.2)

q: Under which provision of R.A. No. 9266 did the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture derive its authority to adopt the Code of Ethical Conduct?
o: Section 29, Article IV
Section 23(f), Article III
Section 7(g), Article II
Section 14, Article I
n: The Board resolved to adopt and promulgate the Code pursuant to Section 7(g), Article II of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: R.A. No. 9266, Sec. 7(g), Art. II)

q: Under Section 9 (Liabilities and Penalties), a violation of the Code may be penalized, at the court's discretion, with a fine within what range?
o: Not less than Php100,000 but not more than Php5,000,000
Not less than Php50,000 but not more than Php1,000,000
A flat fine of Php1,000,000 with no range
Not less than Php10,000 but not more than Php500,000
n: Section 9 provides for a fine of not less than One hundred thousand pesos (Php100,000.00) but not more than Five million pesos (Php5,000,000.00), in addition to or apart from suspension/revocation/cancellation and imprisonment. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 9)

q: Under Section 7.22, an architect shall not discriminate on which grounds, so long as they would not hinder performance of professional work?
o: Race, national origin, age, gender, marital status, religion, or disability
Choice of design software
Years of professional experience only
Membership in a rival professional organization
n: Section 7.22 prohibits discrimination on grounds of race, national origin, age, gender, marital status, religion, or any disability that would not hinder the person's professional work performance. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.22)

q: An architect served as Professional Adviser formulating the program for a design competition. Under Section 7.3, may that architect later enter the same competition as a contestant?
o: Yes, if the competition rules are silent on the matter
Yes, provided the architect discloses the prior role to the organizers
Yes, as long as a different firm submits the entry
No — an architect involved in formulating the program, or engaged as Professional Adviser or Juror, may not enter as a competitor
n: Section 7.3 bars an architect from entering as a competitor in any competition where he/she had direct involvement in formulating the program, or was engaged as Professional Adviser or Juror; similarly, an adviser/juror cannot later be retained as an Architect for that project except as Consulting Architect. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.3)

q: Under Section 4.2, when must an architect acquaint or ascertain from the Client the nature and scope of services and the corresponding professional fees?
o: Only upon project completion, in the final billing
Only after the design development phase is complete
Only when the client asks
At the very inception of the business relationship
n: Section 4.2 requires the architect to acquaint/ascertain the scope of services and inform the client of corresponding fees at the very inception of their business relationship. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.2)

q: Under Section 7.10, an employer-architect's obligations to employees and subordinates include providing a suitable work environment, fair compensation, and what else?
o: Facilitating their professional advancement, and tutoring/mentoring young aspirants toward ethical practice
Guaranteeing lifetime employment regardless of performance
Requiring them to sign non-disclosure agreements before any mentoring
Paying for their board exam review course only
n: Section 7.10 requires providing a suitable work environment, fair compensation, and facilitation of professional advancement, plus tutoring and mentoring young aspirants toward the ideals and ethical practice of the profession. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.10)

q: Under Section 7.15, on what basis should an architect build his/her professional reputation, and what must he/she recognize regarding others' work?
o: Comparisons that discredit rival firms' reputations
Volume of advertising rather than quality of work
Seniority alone, regardless of continuing competence
The merits of his/her own service and performance, while recognizing and giving credit to others for professional work performed
n: Section 7.15 requires building reputation on the merits of one's own service and performance, continuously updating professional know-how, and recognizing/crediting others for professional work performed. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.15)

q: Under Section 7.7, an architect is prohibited from doing what regarding a fellow architect?
o: Maliciously or unfairly criticizing or discrediting another Architect or the latter's work
Publishing an objective comparative case study
Offering constructive peer review at a professional forum
Citing another architect's published work with attribution
n: Section 7.7 simply prohibits maliciously or unfairly criticizing or discrediting another Architect or that architect's work. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.7)

q: Under Section 9, aside from a fine, a violation of the Code may also be penalized with imprisonment for what period, and/or what administrative sanctions?
o: Not less than six (6) months nor more than six (6) years imprisonment, and/or suspension or revocation of the certificate of registration, or cancellation of the special/temporary permit
Community service in lieu of any other penalty
A maximum of 30 days imprisonment only
A mandatory life sentence with no administrative sanction
n: Section 9 provides that violators shall be meted suspension or revocation of the certificate of registration, or cancellation of the special/temporary permit, and/or a fine, or imprisonment of not less than six (6) months nor exceeding six (6) years, or both, at the court's discretion. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VIII, Sec. 9)

q: Under Section 5's introductory statement, the Contractor depends on the Architect to do what?
o: Safeguard fairly the Contractor's interests as well as those of the Client
Represent the Contractor in disputes with the Client
Ensure the Contractor earns the maximum possible profit
Protect only the Client's interests
n: Section 5's chapeau states the Contractor depends upon the Architect to safeguard fairly the Contractor's interests as well as those of the Client. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5)

q: An architect is designing a project within a community that has a historic district and natural heritage features. Under Section 3.1, what is the architect obliged to do?
o: Prioritize the client's aesthetic preferences over any heritage concerns
Defer entirely to the local government's zoning board with no independent duty
Respect and help conserve the community's value system and natural, historic, and cultural heritage, improving the environment sustainably
Avoid the site altogether if heritage features are present
n: Section 3.1 obliges the architect to respect and help conserve the community's values and heritage, and to improve the environment and habitat sustainably, mindful of the widest interests of users. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.1)

q: An architect-employee is leaving his/her employer-architect's firm. Under Section 7.21, may the departing employee take project designs, drawings, or data with him/her?
o: Yes, freely, since the employee personally performed the work
Not without the employer's permission, though the employer may not unreasonably withhold it except to protect legitimate confidentiality
Only with the client's permission, never the employer's
Only if the employee reimburses the firm for materials used
n: Section 7.21 bars a departing architect-employee from taking designs, drawings, data, or other relevant materials without the employer's permission, even if personally performed, while requiring the employer not to unreasonably withhold such permission except where confidentiality must be protected. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.21)

q: The Code of Ethical Conduct was prescribed and issued by which organization, acting as the Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)?
o: The Philippine Institute of Architects
The Professional Regulation Commission directly
The United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP)
The Association of Structural Engineers of the Philippines
n: The Code was prescribed and issued by the United Architects of the Philippines, Inc. (UAP), the IAPOA, by virtue of Board Resolution No. 03, Series of 2004, as approved by the Commission. (Source: Board Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Preamble; Board Res. No. 03, s. 2004)

q: R.A. No. 9266, the law under which the Code of Ethical Conduct is issued, is known by what title?
o: The Professional Regulation Act
The Building Code of the Philippines
The Architecture Act of 2004
The Engineering Practice Act
n: R.A. No. 9266 is known as “The Architecture Act of 2004.” (Source: R.A. No. 9266, Title)

q: Under Section 4.10, what must an architect include in the agreement with the Client regarding dispute settlement?
o: A clause naming the architect as sole arbiter of any dispute
A waiver of the Client's right to dispute any billing
A clause requiring all disputes go directly to court litigation
A clause providing for negotiation, mediation/conciliation, and/or arbitration as alternative methods for settling disputes
n: Section 4.10 requires including in the Client agreement a clause for negotiation, mediation/conciliation, and/or arbitration as alternative dispute resolution methods. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.10)

q: Under Sections 7.18 and 7.19, an architect is called to continuously raise standards in which areas, and to promote what allied field?
o: Only marketing and public relations
Only building code compliance
Aesthetic excellence, functional logic, architectural education, research, training and practice; and to promote the allied arts and construction industry knowledge
Only financial management skills
n: Section 7.18 requires continuously raising standards of aesthetic excellence, functional logic, architectural education, research, training, and practice; Section 7.19 requires promoting the allied arts and contributing to construction industry knowledge and capability. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Secs. 7.18-7.19)

q: Under Section 1 (Traits of Architects), the profession of architecture is said to call for men and women possessing which set of qualities?
o: Purely technical and engineering competence
Only artistic talent and creativity
Strict legal training and litigation skill
Highest responsiveness, business acumen, sensibility, and artistic and technical ability
n: Section 1 states the profession calls for men and women of the highest responsiveness, business acumen, sensibility, as well as artistic and technical ability. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. I, Sec. 1)

q: Under Section 4.7, may an architect undertake the construction of a project for which he/she prepared the plans?
o: Only if the client waives all rights to file a complaint
Only for government-funded projects
No, this is always considered a conflict of interest
Yes, provided it conforms with pertinent sections of the Standards of Professional Practice
n: Section 4.7 permits an architect to undertake construction of a project he/she designed, so long as it conforms with the pertinent sections of the Standards of Professional Practice. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.7)

q: Under Section 7.17, an architect shall not undertake professional work unless the parties have clearly agreed in writing to the terms of the architectural commission. Which of the following is NOT one of the six items listed under 7.17?
o: Any provision for termination
Scope of work
Mode of alternative dispute resolution
The architect's personal educational background
n: Section 7.17 lists six required written terms: scope of work (7.17.1), delineation of responsibilities (7.17.2), any limitation of responsibilities (7.17.3), fee or method of calculating it (7.17.4), mode of alternative dispute resolution (7.17.5), and any provision for termination (7.17.6). The architect's personal educational background is not one of them. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.17 (7.17.1-7.17.6))

q: Under Section 5.5, after promptly inspecting each completed phase of work found to conform with the Contract Documents, what must the architect issue?
o: A revised set of architectural plans
The corresponding Certificates of Payment, and eventually the final Certificate of Completion
A verbal approval only, with no documentation
A notarized affidavit of good workmanship
n: Section 5.5 requires the architect to promptly inspect each completed phase and, if conforming, issue the corresponding Certificates of Payment and, respectively, the final Certificate of Completion. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.5)

q: Under Section 3.4, an architect is barred from paid advertisement and self-laudatory publicity, but may still, without violating the Code, do which of the following and even receive remuneration for it?
o: Pay a publicist to exaggerate his/her project portfolio
Pay for billboard advertisements of his/her design firm
Write books, be a columnist, or participate in seminars/forums advancing public knowledge of the profession
Offer cash incentives to clients who refer new clients
n: Section 3.4 allows an architect to write books, be a regular columnist, contribute literature, or participate in forums/seminars/workshops to advance public knowledge, and to receive remuneration or honorarium for such undertakings. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.4)

q: Under Section 5.4, an architect must reject which kind of offer from a Contractor or Sub-contractor?
o: Legitimate invoices for completed work
Requests for design clarification
Free professional engineering/allied design services, or substantial aid, gifts, commissions, or favors that create an obligation to reciprocate
Standard construction progress reports
n: Section 5.4 requires rejecting offers of free professional engineering/allied design services, or substantial aid, gifts, commissions, or favors from a Contractor/Sub-contractor that would place the architect under an obligation to reciprocate. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. IV, Sec. 5.4)

q: Under Section 6.1, an architect must not solicit free professional/allied design or other technical services from a manufacturer or supplier when doing so would:
o: Save the Client money on the overall project budget
Carry an obligation detrimental to the Client's best interest or adversely affect the architect's professional opinion
Merely require crediting the manufacturer in project documentation
Require the manufacturer to provide product samples
n: Section 6.1 prohibits soliciting such free services when accompanied by an obligation detrimental to the Client's best interest, or one that may adversely affect the architect's professional opinion. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. V, Sec. 6.1)

q: An architect is hired to design an addition to a heritage structure originally designed by another architect. Under Section 7.6, what must the new architect do?
o: Demolish the original heritage elements to avoid design conflicts
Claim full authorship of the entire structure in any publicity
Proceed without notifying anyone since the Client/Owner has changed

Duly notify the original architect of the contemplated project, limit any advertisement/claim to the specific new work if the original mass/design is substantially maintained, and consider restoration possibilities given the heritage value
n: Section 7.6 requires notifying the original architect even where the Client/Owner has changed, limiting the new architect's claim of authorship to the specific added work when the original design predominates, and considering restoration possibilities for structures involving architectural heritage. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.6)

q: Sections 7.11 and 7.12 together describe what obligations toward colleagues, young aspirants, and the profession's advancement?
o: Limit participation in IAPOA to paying dues only
Withhold proprietary techniques from competitors
Unselfishly transfer technical knowledge/experience and foster unity, and unselfishly give time/effort to the profession's advancement through active involvement with the IAPOA
Charge colleagues for any technical advice given
n: Section 7.11 requires unselfishly sharing technical knowledge/experience with colleagues and young aspirants and fostering unity; Section 7.12 requires unselfishly giving time and effort to the profession's advancement through active, personal commitment to the IAPOA. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Secs. 7.11-7.12)

q: Under Section 7.2, donation of professional services as a device for obtaining competitive advantage is prohibited, except for which kind of projects?
o: Worthy civic or religious projects
Any project where a competitor already offered a discount
Any government project regardless of size
Projects for the architect's own family
n: Section 7.2 requires abiding by the Basic Minimum Fee and bars using donated services for competitive advantage, except for worthy civic or religious projects; competitive sketch submissions are also restricted to the Architectural Competition Code framework. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.2)

q: Under Section 4.6, an architect's professional fee billed to the Client should be commensurate with the work, standing, and experience, based upon what prescribed standard?
o: A fee freely negotiated with no reference standard
The government's assessed real property value
The Basic Minimum Fee prescribed under the Standards of Professional Practice
The contractor's project cost estimate alone
n: Section 4.6 ties professional fee billing to the Basic Minimum Fee prescribed under the “Standards of Professional Practice.” (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.6)

q: In the Architect's Credo, whose interest is the architect pledged to hold “over and above my own” when asking for fair remuneration?
o: The government's interest
The contractor's interest
The Client's interest
The architect's own firm's interest
n: The Credo states: “I shall ask for fair remuneration for my professional services from my Client, and hold his/her interest over and above my own.” (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8 (Credo))

q: Under Section 4.4, may an architect guarantee a cost estimate to secure a commission?
o: No, except where provided for by law, such as in certain government projects
No guarantee is ever permitted under any circumstance
Yes, always, to build client confidence
Yes, but only for residential projects
n: Section 4.4 requires explaining the conditional character of estimates; the architect shall not guarantee estimates or cost of work to secure a commission, unless provided for by law (e.g., in certain government projects). (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.4)

q: The Architect's Credo pledges to disclose, whenever required, what kind of personal matter that may create a conflict of interest?
o: Personal medical history
Private business investments or ventures
Personal relationships with subordinates
Personal religious affiliation
n: The Credo states: “I shall disclose, whenever required, any private business investments or ventures that may tend to create a conflict of interest...” (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8 (Credo))

q: Section 7's chapeau describes the architect's moral responsibilities toward which three groups?
o: Foreign architects, banks, and insurers
Contractors, suppliers, and building inspectors
His/her profession, his/her colleagues, and his/her subordinates
His/her family, competitors, and regulators only
n: Section 7 states the Architect has moral responsibilities towards his/her profession, colleagues, and subordinates. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7)

q: The final line of the Architect's Credo pledges consecration to the highest standard of professionalism, integrity, and competence toward which groups?
o: Only the Client and the architect's immediate family
Only future generations of architecture students
The public, the Client, the contractor, the manufacturers/dealers/agents, and colleagues and subordinates
Only fellow IAPOA members
n: The Credo's closing pledge consecrates the architect to the highest standard of professionalism, integrity, and competence to the public, the Client, the contractor, the manufacturers, dealers, and agents, and to colleagues and subordinates as the direct and indirect users/beneficiaries of the architect's services. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8 (Credo))

q: Under Section 2 (Duties and Responsibilities), between which two parties is the Architect charged with exercising mediation and conciliation functions, acting with entire impartiality?
o: UAP and PRC
Client and Contractor
Government and Contractor
Client and Sub-contractor's suppliers
n: Section 2 charges the Architect with mediation/conciliation functions between the Client and the Contractor, requiring entire impartiality. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. I, Sec. 2)

q: A prospective client asks an architect to prepare free preliminary sketches before signing any agreement, in exchange for a chance at the commission. Under Section 4.1, what should the architect do?
o: Provide free sketches only if the client is a repeat client
Provide the free sketches to secure the commission, since it is common industry practice
Decline, since introducing services must be limited to showing prior experience and must not entail free preliminary sketches or services without a compensation agreement
Charge only for materials used, treating design labor as free
n: Section 4.1 limits an architect's introduction of services to presenting examples of prior experience, and prohibits offering free preliminary sketches or other services without a compensation agreement. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.1)

q: As a matter of good citizenship under Section 3.3, an architect must do all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Act in any manner that advances his/her own interest even if detrimental to the profession
Abide by and observe the laws and regulations of government
Comply with the Code of Ethical Conduct and the Standards of Professional Practice
Properly observe laws on the practice of architecture and on planning/design of buildings
n: Section 3.3 explicitly says the architect shall at no time act in a manner detrimental to the best interest of the architectural profession — the opposite of choice d. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.3)

q: By what document number/title is the Code of Ethical Conduct also known, as printed on every page of the source resolution?
o: UAP Document 100: Standards of Professional Practice
IAPOA Document 001
SPP Document 301: Code of Conduct
UAP Document 200: Code of Ethical Conduct
n: Each page of the promulgated Code is footed “UAP Document 200 : Code of Ethical Conduct.” (Source: UAP Document 200)

q: The Code of Ethical Conduct governs registered and licensed architects and holders of what other kind of authorization?
o: Temporary/special permits under R.A. No. 9266
Foreign reciprocity licenses
Apprenticeship certificates
Provisional membership in the UAP
n: The Code applies to registered and licensed architects and to holders of temporary/special permits issued under R.A. No. 9266. (Source: Board Resolution No. 02, s. 2006, Title/Preamble)

q: Under Section 8 (Article VII), when is a registered and licensed architect expected to recite the Architect's Credo?
o: Every time a new project contract is signed
Only during Board of Architecture disciplinary hearings
During special or important occasions, such as mass oath-taking, IAPOA affairs, or PRBOA events
Only once, at the time of initial registration
n: Section 8 requires every registered and licensed architect to recite the Architect's Credo with vigor, passion, and hope during special or important occasions such as mass oath-taking, IAPOA affairs, or PRBOA events. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VII, Sec. 8)

q: Section 4 states the Architect's relationship with the Client is founded on what basic principle, while never sacrificing what higher interest?
o: Strict written contract only; the client's convenience above all else
Confidentiality alone; the contractor's financial interest
Mutual profit maximization; the architect's own reputation
Good faith; never at the expense of higher public interests and public welfare
n: Section 4 provides the Architect-Client relationship is dependent upon good faith, and the Architect must always protect the Client's interests but never at the expense of higher public interests and welfare. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4)

q: Section 6's chapeau states that the exchange of technical information between the Architect and manufacturers/suppliers/dealers of building materials is:
o: Strictly prohibited under all circumstances
Limited to written correspondence only
Permitted only through the UAP's national office
Necessary, and therefore encouraged and commended, subject to conditions
n: Section 6 describes such exchange as necessary and therefore encouraged and commended, subject to the conditions in 6.1 and 6.2. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. V, Sec. 6)

q: A junior draftsman in an architectural firm, without any supervision from the principal architect, prepares a complete set of plans. Under Section 7.9, may the principal architect affix his/her signature and seal to those plans?
o: No — an architect shall not affix signature and seal to plans or documents not done under his/her direct personal supervision
Yes, provided the client consents
Yes, since the draftsman works under the same firm
Yes, as long as the plans are later reviewed briefly before submission
n: Section 7.9 prohibits an architect from affixing signature and seal to any plans or professional documents not prepared under his/her direct personal supervision. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.9)

q: A prospective client asks an architect to begin preliminary design work “just to see how it looks” before any contract is signed. Under Section 7.1, the architect should:
o: Proceed but bill only if the client later signs a contract
Ask a junior staff member to do it off the books
Decline, since professional services must not be rendered, nor preliminary services offered/provided, without a professional service agreement
Proceed informally since no fee is being discussed yet
n: Section 7.1 prohibits rendering professional services without a professional service agreement, and bars offering or providing preliminary services on a conditional basis prior to a definite agreement. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.1)

q: Under Section 4.8, from where must an architect's compensation for services solely come?
o: Referral commissions from contractors
Commissions from material manufacturers
A combination of client fees and supplier kickbacks
The professional fee billed directly to the Client, with no other returns from any other interested source
n: Section 4.8 requires the architect be compensated solely by the professional fee billed directly to the Client, and bars asking for any other returns from any other source. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.8)

q: Under Section 3.2, an architect's civic responsibility toward the public includes what obligation toward his/her professional organization?
o: Only pay membership dues on time
Promote its interests and do his/her full part to enhance its objectives and services
Avoid interacting with other design professions
Refrain from sharing technical information with the construction industry
n: Section 3.2 requires the architect to promote the interest of the professional organization and share in the interchange of technical information with other professions and the construction industry. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.2)

q: Under Section 4.5, an architect must balance the Client's needs and budget against what broader consideration?
o: The profitability of competing firms
The effects of the work upon the life and well-being of the public and community as a whole
The architect's own portfolio marketing needs
The preferences of the general contractor only
n: Section 4.5 requires the architect to consider the Client's needs and budget together with the effects of the work on the public and community, aiming to meet aesthetic and functional requirements commensurate with the budget. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. III, Sec. 4.5)

q: Under Section 3.7, how may an architect display a professional shingle or project billboard?
o: Outside the office or at the project site, in a modest manner, possibly including pictorial reproduction
Only with prior written approval from a competing architect
Only inside the office, never at project sites
Not at all, as any display is considered self-advertisement
n: Section 3.7 permits exhibiting a professional shingle outside the office, or a project billboard with relevant information (possibly including pictures), provided it is done in a modest manner. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. II, Sec. 3.7)

q: An architect possesses substantial information leading to a reasonable belief that another architect has committed a violation of the Code. Under Section 7.20, what is the architect's obligation?
o: Ignore it unless a client is directly harmed
Post the allegation publicly on social media
File a formal complaint with the designated body
Confront the other architect privately and let the matter drop
n: Section 7.20 obliges an architect possessing substantial information supporting a reasonable belief of a Code violation by another architect to file a formal complaint with the designated body. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.20)

q: Section 2 states the Architect's duties and responsibilities extend, beyond the Client, to which other parties?
o: Only the building's future occupants
His/her professional associates, subordinates, and the public
Only competing architects
Only government regulators
n: Section 2 provides the Architect has moral responsibilities to professional associates and subordinates, and is engaged in a profession carrying grave responsibilities to the public. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. I, Sec. 2)

q: A client wants to hire a new architect for a project, but the previous architect was never formally terminated. Under Section 7.5, before undertaking the commission the new architect must:
o: Require the client to sign a waiver absolving the new architect of liability
Wait for the previous architect to file a complaint before acting
Simply proceed since the client has the right to change architects
Notify the other Architect in writing and conclusively determine the original employment was terminated and duly compensated
n: Section 7.5 requires notifying the previously employed Architect in writing and conclusively determining that the original employment has been terminated and duly compensated for, before undertaking the commission. (Source: Code of Ethical Conduct, Art. VI, Sec. 7.5)
